one_liner: Senior program manager running the Architect of the Capitol's Customer Experience Program, using metrics and cross-office projects to improve service for Congress, tenants and Capitol visitors.
fit_summary: Daniel's people skills, comfort with the public and deep knowledge of Congress fit the Capitol Hill setting well. GS-14 requires one full year of experience equivalent to GS-13 in leading a customer service framework for a large organization. Daniel's known background in emergency-management consulting does not show that senior customer-experience program leadership.
eligibility: Open to the public; as a U.S. citizen you meet the AOC citizenship requirement, and no federal status is needed.

You need one full year of specialized experience at the GS-13 equivalent in managing customer service frameworks, systems and strategies for a large organization, creating CX policies and processes, measuring program effectiveness, and running customer-focused training.
There is no education substitution, so experience alone must qualify you at GS-14.
You must pass a drug test, and the clearance is listed as 'Other' (confirm the suitability or background check with HR).
All qualifications must be met by the closing date of November 10, 2026.
strategy: Preview the self-assessment questions first. Rate yourself 'expert' only where your resume shows specific, matching evidence, because HR checks answers against the resume.

Frame your IEM work around government clients as customers. Highlight any stakeholder engagement, client feedback, survivor or applicant service processes, after-action metrics, or training delivery, but only if you actually did them.

On a two-page resume, list for each job the dates (month/year), hours per week, and title. Mirror the four specialized-experience statements in plain language with scale, such as organization size, number of users served, and metrics tracked.
Use the optional cover letter to connect your knowledge of Congress and member offices to serving Members and staffs, while keeping the focus on CX program evidence.

If you can't honestly document a year of GS-13-level CX leadership, apply anyway only as a stretch. In parallel, target GS-9 to GS-12 analyst or constituent and visitor services roles at AOC, the House, the Senate or Library of Congress.
Submit well before 11:59 pm ET on November 10, 2026, and confirm that every required document uploaded.
resume_bullets: Served as [title] at IEM supporting [government client] on [program]; managed client relationships with [number] stakeholders and resolved [type] service issues, improving [metric] by [amount].
Developed [process/procedure/SOP] to collect and analyze [customer/stakeholder feedback data] using [tools]; briefed [audience] on trends and recommended changes adopted in [result].
Designed and delivered [number] interactive training sessions for [audience size/type] on [topic], using [methods] to raise [participation/retention measure].
interview_questions: Describe a time you built or improved a customer service process across several offices. What did you measure?
How would you identify pain points for congressional offices and building tenants?
Tell us about a time you persuaded leaders in other departments to adopt a change you had no authority over.
How would you turn customer feedback data into a recommendation for senior management?
watch_outs: GS-14 is a senior level, and specialized experience likely exceeds your documented background, so there is a real risk of being rated not qualified.
The specialized experience is specific to customer experience, and emergency-management experience alone won't count unless it clearly shows CX framework leadership.
There is a short 18-day window (October 23 to November 10, 2026), a drug test, and an on-site DC commute from Manassas, though telework is available.
